title: Basic CSS styling
brief:
HTML says what things are. CSS says how they look. A CSS rule has a selector (which elements), then properties and values inside curly brackets.

The page is correct but plain. In the CSS box, give the page a background colour, make the h1 a different colour from the text, and make the paragraphs easier to read: at least 18px, with more space between lines.

Keep the text easy to read — dark text on a light background, or light on dark.

vocabulary.gloss: the part of a rule that chooses elements: h1, p, body
what you are changing: color, background-color, font-size
what you change it to: red, #C8102E, 18px
the difference between text colour and background colour; low contrast is hard to read

starterHtml:
Robotics Club

We meet every Tuesday at 5 pm in room B12. Everyone is welcome, even if you have never built a robot.

What we do

We build small robots, write the code that controls them, and enter a competition in spring.

checks.label: The body has a background colour (not white)
The h1 has a colour that is not the default black
Paragraphs have line-height of at least 1.5 (about 27px for 18px text)

hints: Add background-color: #f5f7fa; inside the body rule that is already there.
Add a new rule for h1 with color, for example h1 { color: #C8102E; }
Add a rule for p with two properties: p { font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.6; }
